title: Childhood music: Handy, his father's fiddle and mother's ragtime
summary: Hearing his brother's band, Handy dances, learning Over the Waves, losing his piano in a fire, his mother's training.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Different times. Yeah. You must have learned tunes from your daddy. Oh my lord, yes. Mississippi

Sawyer, all of those things. I can hum them for you. Gambler's Dream, all of those things. Zender. That's a new one on me. My father used to sit down and play those things on a fiddle. And my mother used to play accompaniment on a piano. And by watching her and watching her, I got to where I could do that. Because I've played ever since I was a kid. And my first tune that I ever learned to actually play on the piano was Over the Waves. And my older brother, Dick, that played the harmonica, was the one that taught me how to play it. And from then on I never stopped. But when I was 12 years old and we had moved to the Gulf Coast, I was home burned on the coast and I lost my piano. And that was one of the main reasons why I guess that I never did study because I had no piano to practice on. I never had another piano until I was 24. And the piano I had then was what I bought for $10. So it was a problem. Did you? It made me appreciate 10 times more than to have it shoved down my throat. I shoved it down somebody else's throat, the music that I played. I nearly drove my neighbors crazy. Because I would just, in those days no one locked their doors. And I'd go into somebody else's house and sit down and go to play in the piano. Until finally I got improving, improving, and improving so much that I was invited to come and play. It was tough. But I'll never stop loving it as long as I live. Anything else you want to know?
Your mother you said went to study music. Oh yes, she was a graduate of Cincinnati Conservatory.

I see. She played the style, if you played what they call in those days was ragtime which was Scott Joplin style. She played Dill Pickle and Maple Leaf Rag and all those things. She had all the music to it. I've got the original music on Missouri Waltz and all those kind of things.
